papers.title: Robust PCA Study of TEM Images of Gold Nanospheres: Stable and Dynamic Closed Knot-Like Phase-Space Loops
papers.summary: In this study, we apply Robust PCA to transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images of gold nanoparticles (GNPs) to decompose their geometrical, topological, and dynamical organization into static and dynamic knot-like phase-space loops. Dynamic loops show higher crossing numbers and longer rope lengths, while static loops show higher mean curvature. Although most Alexander determinants were D(t)=1 with isolated values of D(t)=3 at smaller nanoparticle diameters, implying that geometrical complexity does not require topological complexity. The different writhe signs indicate opposite handedness and distinct phase-space geometries in static and dynamic cases. For both static and dynamic knot-like loops, the graphs show an inverse relationship between mean curvature and mean torsion. Flatter trajectories occur at high curvature, and more torsional twisting occurs at low curvature. The small changes in Moffatt-Ricca helicities (~10^-14<<0) are due to circulation-dependent scaling, yet Moffatt-Ricca helicities still follow the same self-linking trend in both static and dynamic configurations. As nanoparticle diameter increases, the dynamic knot-like loops show stronger Kelvin-like spectral localization and smaller minimum self-approach distances, indicating more concentrated spatial modes and tighter geometric folding. At the same time, the decreasing CTEI suggests reduced global phase-space organization. These contrasting trends indicate that the geometrical organization tends to be less global and coherent, and more localized and mode-specific. These results show that the PCA-reconstructed phase space could serve as a mathematical analog to Kelvin's aether, because all disturbances exhibit similar topological configurations with varying degrees of geometric difference.

papers.title: Foundry-Fabricated Silicon Nitride Grating Arrays with Uniform Power Distribution at Visible Wavelengths
papers.summary: Multiplexed optical biosensors are widely deployed to read out many biological targets in parallel. However, their channel count and integration density are limited by the photonic network that delivers light to individual sensing sites. Existing on-chip networks have been largely developed for phased arrays and image projection, where performance is assessed through an aggregate radiation pattern rather than the local intensity at each output. In this Letter, we demonstrate a novel bus-and-tap network architecture for massively parallel multiplexed optical delivery. The network uses cascaded directional couplers with individually designed interaction lengths, allowing for arbitrary, user-defined illumination patterns not possible with conventional binary tree architectures. We experimentally validated our proposed architecture with 46 visible-wavelength grating emitter channels designed for uniform illumination at 40 $\mu$m pitch in a commercial 300-mm silicon nitride foundry process, achieving an emitted-intensity coefficient of variation of 9.3% at 530 nm, and 8.8% under band-integrated illumination from 550 nm to 650 nm. These results provide a route to scalable visible-light delivery for sensing, imaging, neural interfaces, and parallel optical addressing in quantum systems.

papers.title: Black-Hole Ringdown from Photon-Sphere Modes in an Elastic Analogue
papers.summary: Quasinormal modes (QNMs) govern the ringdown of black holes, yet their physical origin and experimental accessibility remain limited. Here we create an elastic analogue of a black hole using a curved metallic shell engineered to emulate a Schwarzschild-like metric, and directly probe its vibrational dynamics in the time domain. Following impulsive excitation, the elastic system exhibits a clear ringdown response, providing a tangible analogue of black-hole ringing. The underlying modes are flexural vibrations localized near the photon sphere. A reduction of the thin-shell elastic equations yields a photon-sphere effective potential and predicts the dependence of the localized-mode frequencies on azimuthal order. Crucially, they persist even when boundary reflections are strongly suppressed, demonstrating that their confinement is governed by a curvature-induced effective potential rather than by cavity boundaries. This platform enables direct access to quasinormal modes through both their temporal decay and spectral signatures, establishing a direct connection between photon-sphere dynamics and ringdown. More broadly, our results identify curvature-induced trapping as a general mechanism for wave localization and dissipation in open systems.

papers.title: QuDPy-FDGF: A Python-Based Tool for Computing Ultrafast Nonlinear Optical Responses Using Frequency Domain Green's Functions
papers.summary: We present QuDPy-FDGF, an open-source Python framework that evaluates Liouville-space pathways as hybrid chains of time propagators and frequency-domain Green's functions. Frequency-resolved intervals are computed directly through shifted linear systems, without time propagation followed by a Fourier transform, while other intervals may remain in the time domain. A model-agnostic block interface separates the physical model from pathway construction, numerical propagation, and detection. The released implementation provides an explicit dense Liouville-space backend for reference calculations and a sector-resolved sparse backend using matrix-free generator actions, Krylov time propagation, and generalized minimal residual (GMRES) resolvent solves. Its observable layer reuses propagated pathway responses to evaluate operator expectation values, action-detected readout interactions, instantaneous jump rates, and integrated mean jump counts. The framework is assessed on an analytically solvable open two-level system and on two examples of increasing complexity: the complete third-order rephasing response, with its eight sequences, of a thermally initialized anisotropic Heisenberg (XXZ) spin chain with unequal excitation sectors, and two coupled dissipative anharmonic modes whose spectra depend on the detected observable, with the fifth-order double-quantum response of their closed limit. The calculations reproduce the analytical two-level response, check the matrix-free sparse evaluation against the dense assembly of the generator, and recover the harmonic-limit cancellation of the fifth-order signal when the required three-excitation manifold is retained. QuDPy-FDGF therefore provides a unified framework for pathway- and observable-resolved nonlinear spectroscopy in finite or truncated Hilbert spaces with unitary or Markovian Gorini--Kossakowski--Sudarshan--Lindblad (GKSL) dynamics.

papers.title: Synthetic Stochastic Time Series from Generative Models
papers.summary: Obtaining statistically converged time-series data represents a fundamental challenge in computational chemistry, where sampling is constrained by the prohibitive computational cost of high-fidelity simulations. The accuracy attainable from a finite simulation budget is governed by the standard-error scaling $1/\sqrt{n}$, rendering exhaustive sampling challenging for systems of realistic complexity. Here we show that generative models trained on high-quality stochastic trajectories can reproduce key statistical properties of the underlying process and generate additional synthetic trajectories at substantially lower computational cost, thereby enhancing the sampling accessible from a finite set of simulations. We present a systematic comparison of four generative architectures across two complementary data sources: an analytically tractable Ornstein-Uhlenbeck reference and donor-acceptor energy-gap trajectories from all-atom molecular dynamics simulations. Among the four architectures tested, the denoising diffusion probabilistic model reproduces the target statistics most consistently, across both data sources and across the range of correlation times examined, and generates far faster than the sequential Transformer. Specifically, for the energy-gap trajectories, augmentation from 0.1 ns of training data yields statistical estimates comparable in accuracy to those obtained from 0.25-0.50 ns of direct MD sampling. We further show that the benefit of synthetic augmentation is bounded by the information contained in the training data, producing a quality floor determined by both the training data and the generative model. Our findings establish diffusion-based generative models as an effective route to data-driven augmentation of stochastic time series in computational chemistry.

papers.title: Predicting droplet landing in angle-controlled surface acoustic wave jetting
papers.summary: Nozzle-free droplet generation eliminates the need for a dispensing orifice, but useful printing also requires control over where droplets are deposited. Here we demonstrate predictable droplet deposition using a nozzle-free, angle-controlled surface acoustic wave jetting platform. Opposing focused interdigital transducers steer droplets from a pendant parent drop toward a collection substrate, with the ejection angle set by the time-integrated acoustic acceleration imbalance. The overall acceleration ratio identifies the operating window for single-droplet ejection and separates it from no-ejection, satellite-droplet, and multiple-droplet regimes. We then connect ejection angle to landing position through a geometric deposition model referenced to a balanced shot in each experiment. At a 5.2 mm parent-drop-to-substrate spacing, 80 steered shots across twenty experiments show strongly anisotropic relative placement scatter: 0.59 mm in the steering direction and 0.06 mm transverse to it. In tests conducted independently over several days, a model calibrated on six earlier collection dates predicted landing positions on two later dates with a root-mean-square error of 0.71 mm; bootstrap resampling placed the 95% confidence range for this error between 0.41 and 1.01 mm. The results establish a practical framework for predicting relative droplet landing in angle-controlled surface acoustic wave jetting and identify the limits imposed by steering angle, separation distance, and actuation regime from an orifice-free, clog-free droplet ejection method.

papers.title: Comparing local and global optimization reveals untapped hybrid potentials for machine learning-based inverse planning
papers.summary: Machine learning (ML) models for normal tissue complication probability (NTCP) can be embedded directly into inverse treatment planning, but the resulting optimization problems are generally nonconvex, and the choice between global and local optimization involves a trade-off between optimality guarantees and computational cost. Two open-source frameworks for ML-based inverse planning were compared: OptiCL (global mixed-integer optimization via constraint learning) and pyanno4rt (local nonlinear optimization via end-to-end differentiation). Logistic regression, linear support vector machine, and feed-forward neural network NTCP models for grade 2+ xerostomia and grade 2+ radiation pneumonitis were embedded. Plan optimization was performed for eight head-and-neck (HN) photon cases and seven lung proton cases. The plans were compared by target coverage, OAR dose metrics, spatial dose agreement, post-hoc predicted NTCP, and runtime. A projection-based gradient approximation was introduced to embed decision trees. In addition to that, warm-starting, constraint strengthening, and pruning were investigated as hybrid strategies for combining local and global optimization. Comparing OptiCL and pyanno4rt across the HN and lung treatment plans revealed broadly consistent dose distributions. Mean differences (OptiCL}$-$pyanno4rt [95% CI]) were small: for HN cases, -0.16 Gy [-0.37, 0.06] (parotid) and -0.00 Gy [-0.01, 0.00] (PTV); for lung cases, -0.52 Gy [-1.10, 0.06] (total lung) and -0.04 Gy [-0.07, -0.01] (PTV). Mean NTCP differences amounted to -0.08 p.p. [-0.49, 0.33] (HN) and -1.73 p.p. [-2.68, -0.77] (lung). OptiCL tended toward lower OAR doses and predicted NTCP, but required higher wall-clock runtime. Hybridization of the decision tree-based HN plan eliminated 80% of binary decision variables without compromising plan quality.

papers.title: Concentration-Dependent Speciation in ZnCl2 Electrolyte Solutions: Transferability of Machine-Learning Interatomic Potentials and Speciation Sensitivity of EXAFS
papers.summary: Predicting speciation in concentrated electrolytes requires accurate ion interactions and adequate sampling of slowly interconverting coordination environments. We combine Zn K-edge extended X-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) measurements with long-timescale molecular dynamics (MD) using machine-learning interatomic potentials to study aqueous ZnCl2 from dilute conditions to 30 m. We train revPBE-based DeepMD models with D3 corrections included or excluded for Zn-containing pairs and compare them with DPMD-SCAN, classical MD (CMD), and MACE-MATPES-r2SCAN. EXAFS calculations are benchmarked against hydrated and chloride-coordinated Zn reference complexes, then applied to MD ensembles alongside Zn-Cl coordination free-energy analysis. Increasing concentration reduces octahedral coordination, replaces water with chloride, and promotes chloride-bridged association. All three DeepMD models yield similar EXAFS at 3 m, but DPMD-SCAN shows greater transferability across concentrations, reproducing measured spectral trends, key features of mixed ZnCl2/LiCl spectra, and octahedral fractions consistent with other studies. DFT treatment strongly affects coordination free energies and aggregation; excluding Zn-related D3 corrections does not systematically improve EXAFS agreement. CMD shows larger spectral discrepancies and less consistent coordination trends. MACE-MATPES-r2SCAN improves upon CMD and yields spectra comparable to DPMD-SCAN, which provides more consistent agreement and greater computational efficiency. Neighbor-resolved analysis shows that distance disorder and scattering-path interference can produce similar EXAFS signatures for distinct coordination ensembles, highlighting the need for rigorous sampling and ensemble-averaged spectra to distinguish isolated from chloride-bridged Zn species.

papers.title: First Results of Calculation of the Dayside Magnetopause Reconnection Rate with TRACERS
papers.summary: Quantifying the rate of reconnection remains a key challenge in the study of geomagnetic storms. In this study, we present the first results from the new Tandem Reconnection and Cusp Electrodynamics Reconnaissance Satellites (TRACERS) mission to calculate the reconnection rate from dispersed ion populations measured in the cusp, using previously developed methodology. We study ion dispersion events in two storms. During the first storm, which occurred on September 30, 2025, 21 dispersion events were identified in TRACERS 2 ion data as a combined result of geospace dynamics and the spacecraft cusp encounters. Throughout this time when ion dispersion was detected by TRACERS , the reconnection rate is calculated and is shown to track reasonably well with another measure of geomagnetic activity, the Cross Polar Cap Potential (CPCP) as obtained by the Super Dual Auroral Radar Network (SuperDARN). The dispersions are correlated with the smoothed CPCP, and a correlation of $r^2=0.62$ was found using the dispersions from the onset and main phase of the storm. The correlation disappears when including dispersions from the recovery period. The distribution of reconnection rates throughout this storm lies generally between 0.1 - 1.5 mV/m, slightly lower than previous reconnection rates calculated with DMSP, but consistent with in-situ observations made with Polar. In this work, we also apply a previously developed automatic identification algorithm for ion-energy cusp dispersion to TRACERS, with the intent that it may serve as a tool for future statistical analysis as the data volume becomes too large to manually review.

papers.title: Laser with $7\times10^{-18}$ stability
papers.summary: We report a laser with record frequency stability, based on a 21 cm cryogenic silicon cavity. For best short-term stability, the cavity operates at 6 K to minimize Brownian thermal noise and achieves a fractional stability of $7\times10^{-18}$ between 2 to 50 s of averaging time and 2.5 mHz linewidth. For best long-term stability the cavity operates at 16 K, where silicon has a zero-crossing of thermal expansion. Slightly increased thermal noise limits the performance to $9\times10^{-18}$, consistent with the expected temperature scaling, but the long-term performance is improved. The laser then has a linewidth of 2.9 mHz and long-term frequency drift less than 4 {\mu}Hz s$^{-1}$. The laser is used to enhance the performance of a state-of-the-art Sr lattice clock, operating with Rabi and Ramsey interrogation times beyond 10 s.

papers.title: Deep-Learning Identification and Global Characterization of Energetic O2+ Beams at Mars
papers.summary: Martian ionospheric ions can be accelerated away from Mars by the solar wind, contributing substantially to atmospheric ion escape. Here, we develop a U-Net-based image segmentation model to identify a distinct population of escaping planetary ions, energetic O2+ beams, from a decade of Mars Atmosphere and Volatile EvolutioN (MAVEN) observations and perform an event-based statistical analysis of their global properties and dependence on external conditions. We find that O2+ beams are widely distributed throughout the Martian plasma environment, with a strong preference for the +E hemisphere, where the solar wind convective electric field points away from Mars. This pronounced spatial asymmetry indicates that the convective electric field plays a major role in beam formation. In the solar wind and magnetosheath, these beams are consistent with the plume. Their occurrence-weighted flux agrees with previous long-term plume estimates, whereas the flux during identified beam intervals is substantially higher. This highlights the advantage of our event-based approach in capturing the intrinsic properties of O2+ plumes. In the induced magnetotail, beam formation remains strongly associated with the convective electric field, while the Hall electric field can provide additional energization. The beam properties are primarily controlled by upstream solar wind conditions, with no apparent influence from solar extreme ultraviolet irradiance. These results might improve our understanding of ion escape at Mars. More broadly, we also demonstrate the potential of deep learning for identifying transient plasma populations from spacecraft observations.

papers.title: Efficient third-harmonic generation in high-Q tantalum pentoxide microcavities
papers.summary: Nonlinear harmonic generation in microcavities offers a compelling route toward energy efficient on-chip short-wavelength coherent light sources, enabled by tight optical confinement within compact mode volumes and flexible dispersion engineering. Tantalum pentoxide (Ta2O5) photonic platforms are particularly promising for realizing such nonlinear processes: their broad transparency window (280-8000 nm) supports broadband operation, their large bandgap suppresses two-photon absorption, and their thick-film deposition capability enables dispersion management--features that can collectively enhance the performance of nonlinear light sources. Here, we demonstrate, to the best of our knowledge, the first efficient third-harmonic generation (THG) in high-Q Ta2O5 microcavities. These microcavities feature smooth surfaces and high loaded Q factors up to 2.67X10^6, thereby facilitating nonlinear interactions. Through dispersion engineering, efficient THG is realized in both suspended microdisks and monolithic microrings under telecom-band continuous-wave laser pumping, as confirmed by optical spectra, visible-light microscopy, and the near-cubic pump-power dependence of the conversion efficiency. This work lays a foundation for chip-scale f-3f self-referencing of frequency combs and next-generation integrated nonlinear photonics.

papers.title: Supercoiling Drives DNA-Protein Co-Condensation
papers.summary: The co-condensation of DNA and proteins plays an important role in genome compaction, including heterochromatin formation and chromosome segregation. Meanwhile, transcription and replication continuously generate DNA supercoiling, yet how the resulting torsional stress affects co-condensation remains poorly understood. Here, by coupling DNA elasticity to a protein concentration field, we show that supercoiling acts as a topological catalyst for co-condensation through a mutually reinforcing interplay with protein wetting. Specifically, protein wetting facilitates twist-to-writhe conversion, generating highly writhed DNA conformations that in turn promote capillary collapse into a protein-rich droplet. In the absence of supercoiling, DNA remains kinetically trapped in metastable extended states within our model, whereas sufficiently strong supercoiling removes the nucleation barrier and enables spontaneous co-condensation. These results establish topology as a distinct control parameter for biomolecular condensation and provide a mechanical framework for how active genomic processes can dynamically regulate large-scale genome organization.

papers.title: Alignment-Free Optical Combining with Scalar-Message Expectation Propagation Detection for Distributed Multi-Aperture Coherent Reception
papers.summary: We propose an alignment-free distributed multi-aperture optical receiver with a single coherent front end, in which the differential delays between apertures are large. The branch signals are optically combined without inter-branch delay or phase alignment. Large differential delays produce separated tap clusters, forming a sparse ISI channel with long memory. Scalar-message expectation propagation exploits this sparsity to recover the transmitted symbols. Simulations show lower BER than equal-area single-aperture reception and no clear BER degradation over the tested delay spans. As the maximum differential delay increases from 100.5 to 200.5 symbol periods, the channel span nearly doubles, while the factor-graph edge count increases by only about 1.5\%. The trade-off is higher BER than ideal coherent combining schemes in exchange for fewer coherent front ends than digital combining and no inter-branch delay or phase alignment before optical combining.

papers.title: Metasurface engineering of transient photothermal responses for vibrational imaging at living interfaces
papers.summary: Chemical transformations at biological interfaces are central to cellular function, yet the weak vibrational signals associated with subtle molecular changes limit their spatially resolved observation. Here, we present metasurface-driven mid-infrared photothermal imaging (MetaMIP), which uses resonantly engineered metasurfaces to amplify molecular temperature modulation while retaining rapid thermal recovery. Visible-light detection converts this response into submicrometre maps of individual nanoparticles and biological cells. In living cells, MetaMIP resolves spatially distinct chemical changes during enzymatic lipid conversion across the cell membrane. These results demonstrate the potential of engineered photothermal interfaces for mapping chemical composition and tracking its evolution during reactions.

papers.title: Experimental evidence of forward energy transfer induced by core-edge coupling in multiscale tokamak turbulence
papers.summary: Turbulence in magnetically confined plasmas is inherently quasi-two-dimensional and can exhibit both inverse and forward energy transfer across scales. Experimental evidence for cross-scale energy transfer in the hot plasma core has, however, remained scarce. Understanding such energy transfer is crucial because it governs turbulent transport, which directly impacts confinement quality of fusion plasmas. Here we report experimental evidence consistent with forward energy transfer associated with core-edge coupling in tokamak turbulence. We combined multichannel collective Thomson scattering (CTS) and radially localized Doppler backscattering (DBS) to resolve cross-scale fluctuation dynamics. The results reveal that a quasi-coherent mode (QCM) originating from the edge is also present in the core and resonantly couples with broadband turbulence, producing significant forward energy transfer and characteristic secondary instabilities. These combined measurements indicate that quasi-two-dimensional tokamak turbulence can support a net energy transfer from ion to electron scales through cross-scale wave-wave interactions, contrary to the inverse cascade paradigm of idealized two-dimensional turbulence. Such a plasma regime is attractive for fusion reactors, as it avoids large edge-localized modes (ELMs) that damage first-wall components and maintains high confinement quality even in the presence of high-Z impurities.

papers.title: From Venus to the Parking Lot: A Flexible Stellar Interferometry Experiment
papers.summary: We describe a simple extension of our earlier Venus interferometry demonstration that can be performed indoors or outdoors, independent of planetary visibility or atmospheric seeing. A small flashlight is placed 15-50 meters away from a telescope and covered with a circular aperture mask (hole diameter 2-6~mm). A small telescope fitted with an opaque mask bearing two 2~mm holes, spaced between 5 and 20~mm apart, is then used to observe interference fringes from this artificial extended source. By varying the hole separation and observing the fringes students can estimate the angular diameter of the source and verify their result directly by simple geometry, a check not possible with astronomical targets. The experiment requires no telescope tracking, no dark skies, and no special equipment beyond materials described in the original paper. It serves equally well as a pre-lab to build intuition before observing Venus, a standalone indoor daytime or outdoor nighttime activity, or a quantitative test of the interferometric method itself.

papers.title: Self-gravitating isothermal equilibria in Eddington-inspired Born--Infeld gravity: exact planar sheets and the Bonnor--Ebert critical mass
papers.summary: We study self-gravitating fluid equilibria in the Newtonian limit of Eddington-inspired Born--Infeld (EiBI) gravity, in which the Poisson equation acquires a term proportional to the Laplacian of the density. We show that this term is equivalent, for arbitrary flows, to an effective pressure $p+\chi\rho^2/8$, so that equilibrium and radial stability reduce exactly to Newtonian problems with a modified equation of state. For pressure-bounded isothermal spheres we compute the EiBI generalization of the Bonnor--Ebert critical mass as a function of the single parameter $\varepsilon=\chi P_{\rm ext}/4c_s^4$, and confirm each change of stability with a radial-pulsation analysis. Near $\varepsilon=0$ the critical mass grows as $M_{\rm BE}(1+5.74\,\varepsilon)$. For $\varepsilon>0.0302$ no isothermal sphere is radially unstable, so a positive EiBI parameter removes the Bonnor--Ebert instability; for smaller positive $\varepsilon$ a stable high-density branch supported by the EiBI pressure follows the unstable one. For $\varepsilon<-0.154$ the mass limit is set instead by the vanishing of the central effective sound speed, and is a loss of equilibrium rather than an instability. In planar geometry the same reduction yields an exact first integral, closed-form isothermal sheets with a maximum column density $2c_s^2/\sqrt{\pi G|\chi|}$ for $\chi<0$, and a complete classification of adiabatic $\gamma=3$ sheets.

papers.title: Core-periphery structure induces double phase transitions in information cascades
papers.summary: Double phase transitions in spreading processes are commonly associated with additional dynamical or structural complexity. Here, we show that such transitions can emerge naturally in prevalent networks exhibiting a core-periphery (CP) organization. Specifically, we consider threshold-driven spreading on CP networks constructed from the stochastic block model, which is characterized by three parameters: the relative core size $r$, the CP coupling strength $\mu$, and the fraction of intra-block link allocation $\alpha$. We find that, by varying the allocation of links between the core and periphery, the system can generate a global cascade window in the parameter spaces, bounded by distinct phase transitions. At the upper boundary, where the periphery becomes sparse, the interplay between the structural inertia (resistance to state changes) of the core and the spreading constraints of the periphery can produce a double phase transition via a two-stage cascading mechanism. This double transition may change type from discontinuous-continuous to discontinuous-discontinuous as the model parameters vary in the limit of a vanishingly small initial seed. Our results reveal a simple structural route to double phase transitions of distinct types and highlight the role of CP structure in shaping threshold-driven spreading dynamics.

papers.title: Reconfigurable Free-Space Optical Interconnects
papers.summary: Free-space optical interconnects can support many low-data-rate channels while avoiding the cost, energy consumption, and packaging constraints of optical waveguide- or fiber-based systems that are widely used today. We propose a free-space optical interconnect system based on reconfigurable micromirror arrays, and show that it scales favorably due to its two-dimensional scaling. We discuss the channel count scaling model, compare our demonstration with theory, and project a channel count above 10,000 to achieve 100 Tbps with slow channels (e.g., <10 Gbps). In a proof-of-concept system with a piston-motion micromirror array, we demonstrate nine channels that are simultaneously optimized. The optimization enables -21.7 dB of average worst-case crosstalk for a channel pitch equal to twice the beam radius, a smaller channel spacing than that required in flat tip-tilt mirrors. The optimization flow is further investigated for different channel spacings, simultaneous illumination, and different numbers of outputs, which generally achieve smaller worst-case crosstalk than the flat tip-tilt mirror case. Overall, the work demonstrates the advantage of piston-motion micromirrors in the proposed optical interconnects.

papers.title: Advancing oxygen-enhanced MRI acquisition and modelling through dynamic ${\Delta}R_{1}$ and ${\Delta}R_2^*$ sensing
papers.summary: Purpose: To develop a multiparametric mapping framework for quantifying fat- and water-specific longitudinal and effective transverse relaxation rates, as well as changes in these parameters induced by a gas challenge. Theory and Methods: The proposed framework, termed SR-Fat DESPOT (single-reference fat-water separated driven equilibrium single-pulse observation of $T_1$), combines a two-component signal model with a single-reference variable flip angle (SR-VFA) approach. The signal model explicitly incorporates gas challenge-induced changes in relaxation rates. The single-reference acquisition strategy reduces data acquisition requirements while preserving sensitivity to both baseline parameters and dynamic changes. Sequence parameters were optimized using Cramer-Rao lower bound theory. SR-Fat DESPOT was evaluated using a modified open-surce abdominal numerical phantom and in two in vivo experiments: a single participant test-retest experiment and a pilot study with six participants. Results: In the abdominal numerical phantom, SR-Fat DESPOT was accurate for quantification of baseline relaxation rates with a normalized median absolute error (nMedAE) 30 when comparing ground truth and estimates. SR-Fat DESPOT was also able to accurately recover median changes in relaxation rates, with differences within 0.001 $s^-1$ when compared to ground truth. In vivo, SR-Fat DESPOT measured changes in relaxation rates for spleen, kidneys, liver, and muscle under 100% O2 breathing, consistent with reports in literature. Changes detected in the spleen and kidneys were statistically significant across participants. Conclusion: SR-Fat DESPOT can quantify changes in relaxation rates induced by a gas challenge while reducing data requirements compared to more conventional approaches used in MR-oximetry literature.

papers.title: Nonlinear Drift Waves and Electrostatic Density Cavities in Upper Ionosphere
papers.summary: Nonlinear drift waves are investigated to explain the mechanism for the creation of one dimensional (1D) and two dimensional (2D) electrostatic density cavities in the presence of density gradient in direction perpendicular to the geomagnetic field. Ion motion along field lines has to be neglected for the formation of density depletion because nonlinear contribution of their parallel motion overcomes the effect of drift waves which create negative nonlinear potential. It is pointed out that a straightforward but appropriate model for drift waves can explain the generation of density cavities having widths in xy-plane if the external magnetic field is assumed to be along z-axis i.e. ${\bf B}_0 = B_0 \hat{z}$. The general nonlinear equation for drift waves takes the form of Zakharov-Kuznetson (ZK) equation when ion nonlinear vorticity term is ignored and it admits the solution in the form of 2D solitary wave. In 1D case, the ZK equation reduces to Korteweg de Vries (KdV) equation which admits solution in the form of 1D soliton. In both cases, the nonlinear potential becomes negative. The order of magnitude of the amplitude and width of density cavities is found to be in agreement with the satellite observations in upper ionosphere.

papers.title: Light pulse propagation through a dielectric slab. II. Two roads to the same field: numerical cross-validation of local (FDTD-ADE) and non-local (retarded integral-equation) solutions
papers.summary: Paper I of this series (arXiv:2610.29336) solves, via the retarded Green's functions, the local differential equations governing light propagation in a plane-parallel dielectric slab, obtaining a pair of retarded integral equations that represent, at the continuum level, the microscopic multiple-scattering picture underlying the local formulation. The two formulations are thus proven to be analytically equivalent. The local system of differential equations is then solved numerically with a finite-difference time-domain scheme (FDTD-ADE). This report closes the loop by solving the retarded integral equations directly, without passing through the local formulation, and comparing the result with the FDTD-ADE solution under the same physical and material conditions. The two independently implemented, structurally different numerical schemes agree within 0.02-1.3% for the reported reflected and transmitted energy fractions; the absorbed fraction, computed independently in both schemes from the Lorentz damping term rather than merely inferred from 1-R-T, agrees closely between the two methods, to the precision reported. Both solutions are also compared with an exact reference, the Airy formula weighted over the pulse spectrum: the direct solution reproduces it to within 0.3%, and its Richardson extrapolation to all digits shown. The agreement persists for a few-cycle pulse and for a sub-wavelength slab, where naive fixed-point iteration of the integral equations is not a practical convergent strategy. A complementary set of movie-style, nine-frame visualizations is also presented, illustrating the same equivalence directly in the field rather than only in integrated observables. To the author's knowledge, a direct numerical cross-validation of these two formulations in this genuinely time-dependent regime has not previously been reported.

papers.title: Stiff source terms inside ADER-DG method
papers.summary: ADER-DG numerical method with the LST-DG predictor, when used to solve hyperbolic equations with stiff source terms, exhibits properties characteristic of IMEX computational schemes. With increasing stiffness, characterized by the parameter $z = \nu{\Delta t}^{n} < 0$, the maximum of the Courant number $\mathrm{CFL}_{\rm max}$ of the ADER-DG numerical method increases. In the region of strong stiffness $|z| \gg 1$, a linear increase in the Courant number $\mathrm{CFL}_{\rm max}(z) \sim |z|$ occurs. In the region of small source terms $|z| \ll 1$, the results $\mathrm{CFL}_{\rm max}(z)$ transform into known results for the problem $\mathrm{CFL}_{\rm max}(0)$ without source terms. In the transition region $|z| \sim 1$, a range of insignificant decrease in the Courant number $\mathrm{CFL}_{\rm max}(z)$ is discovered. In the linear case, instability is violated precisely when one of the matrix eigenvalues reaches $\lambda = -1$, regardless of the phase $\theta$ of the numerical solution. A rigorous stability theory of the ADER-DG numerical method for stiff problems for arbitrary degree $N$ of basis polynomials is constructed. The stability condition is simplified to solving a polynomial equation for the Courant number $\mathrm{CFL}$. Highly accurate dependencies of the Courant number $\mathrm{CFL}_{\rm max}(N, z)$ of the ADER-DG method on the parameter $z$ are obtained. A rigorous direct proof of the approximation of the ADER-DG method is presented. Approximation orders $p = N+1$ for arbitrary degrees $N$ are rigorously derived. A set of numerical experiments is carried out to apply the ADER-DG method to solving both a linear advection-reaction equation and the system of Euler equations for a two-component reacting medium. The results obtained in these calculations confirm the theoretical results well.

papers.title: All-photonic millimeter-wave and terahertz signal core at room and cryogenic temperatures
papers.summary: Millimeter-wave and terahertz technologies offer new opportunities for high-capacity communications, sensing, and quantum systems, but electronic signal chains above 100 GHz are limited by weak sources, noisy receivers, and lossy interconnects. Photonic approaches mitigate these constraints by enabling chip-scale high-frequency components, yet existing implementations generally retain lossy off-chip electrical or free-space links, hindering dense and compact integration for cryogenic or space-constrained settings. Here, we show a monolithic lithium tantalate photonic chip, termed a signal core, which generates, modulates, routes, and detects continuous-wave signals at discrete frequencies between 100 GHz and 2.5 THz. The architecture integrates high-frequency functional modules on chip and uses exclusively fiber-based optical interfaces. Bidirectional coherent electro-optic conversion enables signal generation, detection, and nanosecond-scale amplitude and phase modulation, while micro-coplanar striplines interconnect the modules into an end-to-end signal chain on a single chip. Our modules achieve single-photon electro-optic coupling rates of g_0/2\pi=10 kHz and peak drive-power-normalized photon-flux conversion efficiencies of 1.0%/mW for generation and 0.5%/mW for detection. It also operates at 4 K in a dilution refrigerator through the same fiber-only optical links. Together, these capabilities establish an all-photonic platform for millimeter-wave-to-terahertz systems and offer a broadly applicable architecture for applications constrained by electrical-interconnect loss, heat load, and footprint.

papers.title: Laser-design methodology for extending an available wavelength range of dual-wavelength injection-seeded laser
papers.summary: This paper describes a method for expanding the applicable wavelength range of dual-wavelength oscillation injection-locked lasers. Special focus is placed on the laser design that enables simultaneous oscillations at both the gain center and gain tail, requiring the most stringent requirements. We show that a sufficient performance can be achieved by introducing a wavelength-dependence property onto the output coupling mirror, without giving any losses in the laser resonator. We also show how we can determine such wavelength-dependent property on the basis of experimental measurements. Using the designed output-coupler, in practices, we demonstrate simultaneous oscillations with an equal output power, across a variety of wavelength combinations of near the gain center and around the gain tail in which the wavelength separation amounts 60 nm at the most.

papers.title: Intrinsic Angular Momentum Contribution to the Sagnac Response of a Rotating Helical Optical Fiber
papers.summary: We investigate rotation-induced phase accumulation of structured light in a mechanically rotating uniform helical optical fiber using a four-component optical Dirac-like equation. In the paraxial and weak-geometry regime, the intrinsic dynamics contain a torsion-induced geometric coupling and a mechanical rotation--angular-momentum coupling. We show that, in a common-path mirror-reflection geometry, both the torsion-induced geometric phase and the conventional area-dependent Sagnac contribution cancel over a complete round trip, whereas the intrinsic rotation--angular-momentum phase survives. The surviving phase depends on the intrinsic total angular momentum of the structured optical mode and provides a common-path interferometric route for probing intrinsic angular momentum effects in rotational sensing.

papers.title: LieGROG: A Lie algebra approach for calibrating GRAPPA operators
papers.summary: Purpose: In multi-coil acquisitions based on non-Cartesian k-space sampling, image reconstruction using GRAPPA Operator based gridding (GROG) can provide advantages with respect to the non-uniform FFT (NUFFT): It waives both the need for calculating a density compensation function, and for transferring back and forth between Cartesian and non-Cartesian points in iterative algorithms. Non-trivial noise propagation and self-calibration limited to specific trajectories, however, have contributed to GROG being rather sparsely applied so far. Theory and Methods: The group structure of the GRAPPA Operator allows estimating its generator as a single joint fit for all k-space dimensions within the associated Lie algebra. Assuming a linear regime, the generator can be fitted using subsequent pairs of sampling points from nearly any arbitrary non-Cartesian read-out. This approach called LieGROG was evaluated against classical GROG calibration and NUFFT/Toeplitz, using simulations with an analytic ground truth and various 2D and 3D MR-scans employing typical non-Cartesian trajectories. Results: Throughout all applications, LieGROG proved to provide fast, robust and straightforward calibration of the GRAPPA Operator. It clearly outperformed the classical GROG calibration approaches in terms of noise amplification. LieGROG matched the results of the NUFFT/Toeplitz-based reference MR reconstructions closely, while being 6 to 189 times faster and reducing peak VRAM by 20 to 45% in the 3D experiments. Conclusion: LieGROG transforms GROG into a more versatile and stable tool, ultimately aligning non-Cartesian imaging with the standard, FFT-based reconstruction pipelines established for Cartesian scans.

papers.title: A Personal History in Quantum Foundations: an Oral History Interview
papers.summary: This oral history interview provides Yakir Aharonov's personal and conceptual recollections from the 1950s to the 2000s, focusing on his academic trajectory, some of his major contributions to quantum foundations, and his perspective on the development of the field. The interview traces Aharonov's academic career through the Technion, University of Bristol, Brandeis University, Yeshiva University, University of South Carolina, Tel Aviv University, George Mason University, and Chapman University. The interview also traces the development of Aharonov's work and collaborations on the EPR paradox, time-energy uncertainty relations, quantum measurement theory, quantum frames of reference, the two-state vector formalism, weak values, protective measurements, and several other contributions. It includes recollections of meetings and discussions with David Bohm, Niels Bohr, John Clauser, Paul Dirac, Rudolf Peierls, Aage Petersen, and Abner Shimony. Also mentioned: David Albert, Jeeva Anandan, Peter Bergmann, Gideon Carmi, Avshalom Elitzur, Dave Finkelstein, Vladimir Fock, Itzhak Kalugai, Ed Lerner, Joel Lebowitz, Stanley Mandelstam, Yuval Ne'eman, Sandu Popescu, Maurice Pryce, Daniel Rohrlich, Nathan Rosen, Joseph Safko, Paul Singer, Daniele Struppa, Leonard Susskind, Lev Vaidman, Chien-Shiung Wu.

papers.title: Efficient Modeling of 3D-Printed Freeform Waveguides with a Transformation Optics-Based Beam Propagation Method
papers.summary: An efficient numerical method is introduced for simulating wave propagation in 3D-printed freeform waveguides, referred to as photonic wire bonds (PWBs). This approach integrates transformation optics (TO) with curvilinear meshing to map the original 3D freeform PWB structure onto a straight waveguide, which possesses anisotropic material characteristics. The resulting waveguide is then analyzed using an anisotropic full-vectorial beam propagation method (BPM). To validate the performance and effectiveness of the proposed TO-BPM algorithm, a comparison is made with the finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) technique. Our approach reduces the simulation time by more than two orders of magnitude, depending on the degree of trajectory bending, in combination with a mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 3.9% in power transmission simulation relative to the FDTD.

papers.title: On Spurious Mesh-Scale Oscillations Associated with Resonance-Cone Regimes in Wave-Plasma Simulations
papers.summary: Spurious mesh-scale oscillations can compromise frequency-domain finite-element simulations of electromagnetic wave propagation in magnetized cold plasmas. We investigate their origin and mitigation through a verification framework combining a mixed N\'ed\'elec-Lagrange solver, a waveport accommodating non-orthogonal modes in anisotropic media, and an analytical generalized Fresnel benchmark at a vacuum-plasma interface. Comparisons with this benchmark show that the observed oscillations occur in resonance-cone regimes and are absent from the analytical fields, confirming their numerical origin. Systematic tests assess the effects of approximation order, variational formulation, mesh geometry, and numerical collisionality. Plane-wave residual and Fourier spectral analyses suggest that local mesh variations induce spectral coupling to additional wavevector components, predominantly populating the dispersion branches in collisionless resonance-cone regimes where the reduced scalar equation loses ellipticity. Uniform rectangular grids recover the analytical wave structure, further supporting the role of mesh geometry and symmetry. However, strict symmetry requirements limit the applicability of this approach, motivating numerical regularization. In resonance-cone regimes, introducing sufficient numerical collisionality suppresses the mesh-scale oscillations, yielding smooth electric-field solutions and reducing the error relative to the analytical benchmark. For one resonance-cone benchmark configuration, the error-minimizing damping decreases with mesh refinement according to an empirical $Z_{\mathrm n}\propto h^{1.48}$ scaling, sustaining error reduction consistent with second-order convergence and avoiding the accuracy limit imposed by fixed collisionality. ...

papers.title: Effective-action formulation of $\mathbf{k}$-odd bianisotropy and unidirectional polarization rotation in nonlocal temporal metamaterials
papers.summary: We derive the effective action of temporal metamaterials up to first order in spatial derivatives through a multiscale analysis of the electromagnetic Lagrangian density. We show that the first-order spatial correction gives rise to an effective bianisotropic coupling tensor that is odd in the wavevector $\mathbf{k}$. Remarkably, chiral, pseudochiral, and omega-type bianisotropic responses emerge as distinct directional manifestations of a single nonlocal coupling tensor, even when the underlying electric and magnetic response tensors remain symmetric. Furthermore, we establish a framework for analyzing Lorentz reciprocity based on the Hessian of the effective action. We demonstrate that Lorentz reciprocity is preserved in the presence of omega-type coupling but is broken when chiral or pseudochiral coupling emerges. This nonreciprocity manifests as the unidirectional rotations of normalized Stokes vectors incurred by Floquet-engineered chirality and pseudochirality.

papers.title: The Mechanism of Chirality in Plasmonic Structures: Asymmetric Resonance Modes
papers.summary: This study presents a theoretical framework for understanding the mechanism of chirality generation and circular dichroism (CD) in chiral nanostructures, with a particular focus on the role of asymmetric plasmon resonance mode distributions. Although previous studies have linked chiroptical properties to resonance differences, the specific nature and origin of these differences have not been fully elucidated. Here, we provide a more detailed explanation by quantitatively analyzing the asymmetric electric-field components arising from mode asymmetry. Specifically, we examine the near-field symmetry of individual nanorods and corner-stacked coupled structures (CSCS). The results demonstrate that chirality arises from asymmetric electric-field distributions, which give rise to distinct phase and amplitude responses of the electromagnetic fields in the composite structure under right-handed circularly polarized (RCP) and left-handed circularly polarized (LCP) illumination. The absorption and CD spectra, which exhibit distinct features around $910\,\mathrm{nm}$, support this mechanism and provide valuable insights into the design of chiroptical materials. The proposed mechanism is not restricted to a specific chiral structure or resonance and offers a broader explanation for the generation of circular dichroism.

papers.title: Spatial scaling of network length and shared-node density in bilayer distribution grids
papers.summary: Certain distribution networks are built in layers, each layer collecting a commodity from the layer above it and delivering it to the layer below. We propose a minimal model that gives the length of each layer per unit area from the local density of demand, here the population density. Starting from the Beardwood, Halton and Hammersley law for minimal networks, the length of a layer depends on the number of nodes it reaches and on the area occupied by the users. When two consecutive layers share this area, the gap between their two length exponents is fixed by the exponent of the density of their shared nodes, with no adjusted parameter. We test the model on the complete low and medium-voltage grid of metropolitan France, at the resolution of a population raster. The exponents are fitted by Poisson maximum likelihood on every pixel, with confidence intervals from a spatial block bootstrap. The length exponents imply an effective settled area that grows sublinearly with the density, and the gap between them agrees with the exponent of the substation density, counted independently. The agreement holds over the whole territory, so that the model can serve to estimate the length of such networks where only the density of demand is known.

papers.title: Conditional Mean Flows for Frequency-Domain Scattered Wavefield Generation
papers.summary: Frequency-domain wavefield modeling underpins seismic imaging and inversion, where repeated Helmholtz solutions become costly as velocity models, source locations, and frequencies vary. Neural operators learn mappings between physical fields, and their accuracy can decline outside the training distribution. Diffusion models learn wavefield distributions and generally require repeated sampling evaluations to produce accurate fields. A conditional mean flows model is introduced for complex scattered-wavefield generation. The analytical background wavefield serves as a condition alongside the velocity model, supplying spatially organized information about the source location and frequency. Learning the scattered wavefield avoids the point-source singularity in the target and supports generalization across these physical conditions. The model estimates the average transport velocity over a finite interval connecting Gaussian noise to the scattered field. This representation captures the accumulated displacement and permits both full-interval one-step generation and interval-partitioned sampling. Trained on OpenFWI, the model is evaluated on in-distribution and out-of-distribution velocity structures, frequency generalization, and inference efficiency. In most evaluated settings, one-step mean flows sampling achieves lower wavefield error than multi-step diffusion. Because each sampling step requires another network evaluation, accurate one-step generation also reduces inference time. These results indicate that mean flows can provide accurate and efficient frequency-domain scattered-wavefield generation.

papers.title: Extended-regularized lattice Boltzmann method
papers.summary: Regularized lattice Boltzmann methods improve numerical stability by projecting the nonequilibrium distribution onto its hydrodynamic second-order Hermite sector and filtering the remaining kinetic modes. We introduce a separate relaxation time for the complete complementary kinetic subspace. The resulting extended-regularized lattice Boltzmann method (E-RLBM) interpolates continuously between the Bhatnagar-Gross-Krook and regularized collision operators while retaining a two-rate implementation. A Chapman-Enskog expansion shows that the isothermal Navier-Stokes equations are recovered with kinematic viscosity $\nu=c_s^2(\tau-\Delta t/2)$, independently of the kinetic relaxation time $\tau_{\rm nh}$, whereas $\tau_{\rm nh}$ changes higher-order truncation errors. For linear transverse shear, its first effect is a fourth-derivative term whose coefficient depends on the direction of propagation relative to the lattice. This fourth-order coefficient is affine in $\tau_{\rm nh}$. For linear shear on D2Q9 and $\tau_{\rm nh}$ between $\tau$ and $\Delta t$, it lies between the corresponding BGK and RLBM values in every propagation direction. Stability maps for the decaying Taylor-Green vortex and flow past a rectangular obstacle show that an appropriate kinetic relaxation substantially enlarges the stable parameter domain. In a Taylor-Green convergence test with consistent initialization, all three operators converge at second order, and their error differences follow the hyperviscous coefficient for diagonal shear waves: the E-RLBM error is about 6% above the BGK error and about 40% below the RLBM error; in a double shear layer at Re = 80000, the E-RLBM follows the RLBM convergence curve. The proposed collision operator therefore provides a low-cost means of controlling nonhydrodynamic modes without introducing a full multiple-relaxation-time basis.

papers.title: In situ performance of the Vertex Silicon Plane in the BM@N experiment during Run 9
papers.summary: The Vertex Silicon Plane (VSP) was commissioned and operated for the first time as the most upstream tracking station of the Baryonic Matter at Nuclotron (BM@N) experiment at the NICA accelerator complex during Run 9. The station consisting of six double-sided silicon microstrip modules based on the CBM-BM@N detector technology was installed about 8 cm downstream from the target inside the SP-41 analyzing magnet. The in situ module performance was characterized in terms of the signal-to-noise ratio, time resolution, and Lorentz drift in the magnetic field. The most probable cluster signal-to-noise ratio ranges from 15.5 to 33.2, while the time resolution relative to the trigger pulse is about 12 ns. The tracking performance was evaluated using track-hit residuals and hit-matching efficiency; two independent reference configurations based on the Forward Silicon Detector (FSD) and Gas Electron Multiplier (GEM) tracking systems give consistent efficiencies of about 95%. The contribution of the VSP to the BM@N tracking performance was further studied through the transverse track impact parameter and the reconstruction of short VSP-GEM tracklets. Owing to its position close to the target and its coverage at large polar angles, the VSP provides an additional near-target tracking point and makes it possible to extend the geometrical acceptance beyond that of the FSD- and GEM-based central tracking system.

papers.title: GeoAgent: Contract-Constrained LLM Agents for Seismic Data Processing
papers.summary: Large language models (LLMs) can drive scientific software through function calling, but free-form tool use is fragile on long, data-dependent processing chains. Models omit arguments, invent units, feed the previous artifact into the wrong input, and report completion without a verifiable product. We present GeoAgent, an agent system for seismic data processing built on Madagascar's roughly 1{,}965 command-line programs. GeoAgent exposes 54 operator agents (51 generated from a declarative specification), retrieves from an index of 1{,}937 operators, and encodes the processing flow as a nine-stage state graph. Four explicit contracts---named artifacts, input resolution, parameter takeover, and artifact validation---move everything the graph can determine out of the model's discretion. A deterministic geometry tool parses the self-describing SPS/RPS/XPS and SEG-Y headers, cross-checks eight consistency conditions, and reproduces the reference shell recipe exactly. The system runs in containers with session- and task-level isolation, bounded execution, and defenses against silent failures. On a 2-D land dataset, the nine-stage pipeline completes in about six to eleven minutes and yields a verified artifact at every stage, while retrieval reduces per-turn tool context from about 12k to 2k tokens. We report the design, deployment experience, and motivating failure modes.

papers.title: Influence of nanoparticle shapes in nanofluid film boiling on vertical cylinders: A numerical study
papers.summary: This research explores how nanoparticle shapes affect the thermal behavior of nanofluid film boiling along a vertical cylinder, using a Continuous-Species-Transfer method within a Computational Multi-Fluid Dynamics framework. The behavior of nanoparticles in both liquid and vapor phases is modeled, accounting for Brownian motion and thermophoresis. A comprehensive two-dimensional axisymmetric analysis is conducted to investigate the effects of various Al2O3 nanoparticle shapes, including spheres, bricks, blades, cylinders, and platelets, on boiling heat transfer. The results demonstrate that nanoparticle shape has a minimal impact on deposition dynamics but significantly affects kinematic viscosity, particularly for platelet-shaped nanoparticles. Blade-shaped nanoparticles provide substantial enhancement of thermal transport, as indicated by pronounced temperature gradients and increased thermal conductivity. These nanoparticles also improve the Nusselt number, suggesting enhanced boiling heat transfer efficiency. This improvement is particularly significant at higher nanoparticle concentrations, although the relationship is not strictly linear. Future work will explore different nanoparticle materials, boiling scenarios, and experimental validation.

papers.title: Unconstrained learning of equivariant atomistic properties
papers.summary: Machine-learned interatomic potentials based on graph neural networks (GNNs) have made first-principles accuracy routine for the potential energy surface (PES). Their backbones, often O(3)-equivariant by design, are increasingly used to learn other atomistic properties. Many of these are of high angular order or pseudotensorial character, defined per atom, or expanded on large atom-centered basis sets. Such targets strain equivariant GNNs, whose tensor products grow steeply in cost with angular order and can fail to represent the target if truncated, forcing difficult trade-offs between hyperparameters. Unconstrained models like the Point-Edge Transformer (PET) instead replace explicit O(3) algebra with edge-to-edge attention and learn equivariance from data, so that the same backbone can in principle learn any equivariant property. We demonstrate how to use PET to learn molecular dipoles and polarizabilities, NMR chemical shielding tensors, and auxiliary-basis expansions of the electron density. Increasing the backbone size systematically improves both accuracy and equivariance error, and targeted architectural and training choices reduce the symmetry breaking further. PET matches or improves on the released reference models at lower inference cost and, compared with equivariant models, a smaller memory footprint. The predictions give accurate IR and Raman spectra and isotropic shieldings; the predicted densities accelerate self-consistent field calculations and give one-shot ground-state properties, and pretrained density models transfer to higher levels of theory by fine-tuning on little data. The impact of approximate equivariance is small for most observables, further validating this approach to train fast, accurate, and useful surrogate models for properties beyond the PES.

papers.title: Shaping Near Fields of Photonic Modes into Topological Textures
papers.summary: Topological textures of light, such as optical vortices and skyrmions, are attractive for high-density information encoding and light-matter interactions. In the near field, topologies have primarily been realized using polaritonic platforms that inherently tie the platform to the material dispersion, limiting their footprint due to propagation losses and restricting their operating spectral region. Here, we introduce a route to shape near-field topologies through the geometric engineering of a dielectric metasurface supporting a quasi-bound state in the continuum resonance, without the need for polaritonic surface waves. In-plane deformation of our metasurface bars conserves their resonance-driven near-fields locally, so that the metasurface geometry and the polarization of the illuminating light dictate the generated topology. By shaping silicon unit cells into geometries with rotational symmetry, we create optical topologies with controllable topological charge. Using phase-resolved scattering-type near-field optical microscopy, we experimentally characterize high-purity resonance-locked topologies such as vortices in concentric rings and topological charge doublets in Archimedean spirals. In contrast to conventional topological textures, our purely photonic mode-based field textures are stationary standing waves in the radial direction, without relying on surface-wave propagation or polaritonic dispersion, establishing a spectrally and spatially scalable platform for near-field topological photonics.

papers.title: Quartz Crystal Microbalance impedance of discrete adsorbates with lubricated contact
papers.summary: We present a thorough theoretical investigation of the shear force exerted on a horizontal plate undergoing fast (MHz range) longitudinal oscillations in presence of a spherical particle suspended in the liquid at close proximity to the plate. This hydrodynamic problem is relevant toward the analysis of frequency response (i.e., complex impedance) of Quartz Crystal Microbalance (QCM) to discrete (particulate) adsorbates. For low areal density of adsorbates, the contributions of individual particles remain additive, rendering the theory applicable towards quantitative interpretation of the experimental measurements. For adsorbates much smaller than the viscous penetration depth, the closed-form analytical expressions for the complex impedance were derived for particles of arbitrary density, assuming a lubricated contact (i.e., non-localized adsorption). The theoretical predictions were shown to be in an excellent agreement with accurate Finite Element numerical computations. The validity of the theoretical approach was confirmed by QCM measurements conducted for polystyrene nanoparticles in a broad range of sizes, from 32 nm to 510 nm, adsorbing onto gold/silica sensor upon varying the oscillation frequency.

papers.title: Fock-space relativistic coupled-cluster study of systematic shifts and fine-structure constant sensitivity in {\rm Cf$^{17+}$}, {\rm Cm$^{15+}$} and {\rm Bk$^{16+}$} highly charged ions
papers.summary: Highly charged ions (HCIs) are among the most promising candidates proposed for the development of next-generation optical clocks and the precision tests of fundamental physics. In this work, we investigate the clock-relevant properties of $\rm Cf^{17+}$, $\rm Cm^{15+}$ and $\rm Bk^{16+}$ HCIs using Fock-space relativistic coupled-cluster (FSRCC) theory. The corrections from Breit interaction, QED effects and perturbative triples are incorporated to improve the accuracy of results further. We compute excitation energies, transition amplitudes, lifetimes, hyperfine structure constants, electric quadrupole moments, and electric dipole polarizabilities for low-lying states of these ions. These properties are further used to characterize important clock transitions and estimate key systematic frequency shifts. Our calculations reveal that the proposed clock transitions exhibit strongly suppressed systematic frequency shifts. We also compute the sensitivity coefficients, $q$, and enhancement factors, $K_{\alpha}$, for the proposed clock transition as a probe to variation in the fine-structure constant, $\alpha$. Our calculations predict exceptionally large $K_{\alpha}$ of $-55.3$ and $57.5$ for $5f_{5/2} \rightarrow 6p_{1/2}$ transition in $\rm Cf^{17+}$ and $6p_{1/2} \rightarrow 5f_{5/2}$ transition in $\rm Bk^{16+}$, respectively. These giant $K_{\alpha}$s place the proposed transitions among the most sensitive optical probes for the laboratory searches for $\alpha$ variation. Further, a comparative analysis of proposed transitions in $\rm Cm^{15+}$ and $\rm Bk^{16+}$ shows that, $5f_{5/2} \rightarrow 5f_{7/2}$ transition possess smaller systematic shifts and is therefore attractive for precision frequency metrology, whereas $6p_{1/2} \rightarrow 5f_{5/2}$ transition exhibit significantly enhanced sensitivity to $\alpha$ variation.

papers.title: Precise Determination of Electric Dipole Polarizabilities of Sr Clock States Using Linear-Response and Equation-of-Motion Relativistic Coupled-Cluster Methods
papers.summary: We present accurate values of the electric dipole polarizabilities ($\alpha$) of the ground and excited states of Sr using four-component relativistic coupled-cluster (RCC) theory within the linear-response (LR) and equation-of-motion (EOM) frameworks. We first investigated accuracy of the ground-state polarizability using the LR-RCC method in both spherical and Cartesian coordinate representations. Upon obtaining consistent results for the ground state, we determine the polarizabilities of the excited states using the EOM-RCC method within the finite-field approach. The uncertainties in our results are assessed by examining the completeness of the basis set, higher-order relativistic corrections, and contributions from higher-level excitation configurations beyond the truncation in our RCC method. We also discuss various procedures for extrapolating contributions to the complete basis set limit and examine their respective limitations. Our calculated ground-state polarizability is found to be inconsistent with the latest atomic calculation, but agrees with other calculations and experimental value. Using the differential $\alpha$ value from the EOM-RCC method, we estimate the fractional black-body-radiation-induced frequency shift of the Sr $^{1}$S$_{0}$$\rightarrow$$^{3}$P$_{0}$ clock transition to be $-5.40\times10^{-15}$.

papers.title: Cleaner air strengthens the Pacific trade winds without a detectable change in El Nino
papers.summary: Air quality policy will cut aerosol and ozone precursor emissions, and studies disagree on how the tropical Pacific circulation and the El Nino Southern Oscillation (ENSO) will respond. Here we show, in 12 Earth system models with and without air quality controls, that the cuts strengthen the Pacific trade winds and offset half to two thirds of the weakening projected without them. The response is absent with prescribed sea surface temperatures and detectable only after 2040. It is consistent with the Indian Ocean warming relative to the Pacific, which also ranks the responses to cuts made region by region. ENSO amplitude changes by less than a tenth of its value, the smallest change this ensemble could detect. The change implied by the mean state shift is a sixth of that, and an ENSO model trained without the reduced emission runs predicts none. El Nino's regional impacts still change, because the background climate does.

papers.title: AI Enhanced Cerenkov Luminescence Microscopy
papers.summary: Cerenkov Luminescence Microscopy (CLM) enables the visualization of radiotracer uptake in three-dimensional (3D) tumor spheroids but is limited by low photon statistics and spatial blurring caused by positron transport. Here, we present a Monte Carlo (MC)-guided deep learning framework for CLM image restoration. Using TOPAS/Geant4, we developed a physical model of heterogeneous 3D tumor spheroids to simulate positron transport, Cerenkov photon generation and optical propagation. A dataset of 15,360 paired degraded and idealized ground-truth (GT) images was generated from 80 simulated spheroid geometries and used to train a supervised Content-Aware Image Restoration (CARE) network. Compared with the self-supervised Noise2Void (N2V) denoising method, CARE achieved substantially lower reconstruction errors on synthetic validation data, reducing the mean squared error from 0.0492 to 0.0051. Training stability and noise robustness analyses further demonstrated high reproducibility of the restored images. The trained CARE model was subsequently applied to experimental CLM images acquired from 27 U87 tumor spheroids following 18F-FDG uptake. The restored images exhibited more localized intensity distributions and higher local contrast and signal-to-noise ratios compared with raw and N2V-processed images. These findings, aligned with the 3Rs principles of animal experimentation, demonstrate the potential of physics-based supervised restoration to mitigate both noise and positron-induced spatial broadening in CLM.

papers.title: Second- and third-order nonlinearities in silicon nitride waveguides via heterogeneous integration of lithium niobate membranes
papers.summary: Thick, dispersion-engineered silicon nitride is a leading platform for integrated third-order nonlinear optics, supporting supercontinuum and frequency comb generation. However, it lacks the second-order nonlinearity required by many applications. Here we bond pre-fabricated x-cut thin-film lithium niobate membranes onto finished silicon nitride waveguides as a back-end step, compatible with commercially fabricated waveguides. A single silicon nitride waveguide generates an octave-spanning supercontinuum and, through the lithium niobate membrane, concurrent second-harmonic, sum- and difference-frequency generation. These results open new possibilities for thick silicon nitride photonics, from visible light generation to on-chip $f$-$2f$ comb self-referencing, a key step towards miniaturised timing and navigation quantum technologies.

papers.title: Extracting target-related flow structures using a time-lagged cross-correlation ranking criterion
papers.summary: Structures with large global contributions to a flow field are not necessarily those that are most closely associated with a specified engineering observable. We propose a time-lagged cross-correlation (TCC) ranking criterion to extract target-related dynamical structures from a fixed modal expansion while preserving existing spatial modes and temporal coefficients. The criterion ranks mode groups by the mean squared norm of cross-responses between their flow contributions and the observable over a lag window. It is tested separately using dynamic mode decomposition (DMD) and proper orthogonal decomposition (POD). TCC-DMD analysis shows that TCC recovers three low-contribution target structures from a dominant background in a synthetic flow. The reconstruction error for the target subfield is 2.15\%. In the cylinder wake, different force observables select structures associated with the vortex-shedding fundamental, slow drag variations, and the second harmonic. In the cavity case, selected modes connect two main frequency bands of the target observable to distinct spatial amplitude and phase distributions. TCC-POD analysis shows that the criterion minimises the weighted truncation error of the correlation operator among equally sized subsets of the fixed orthogonal basis. A comparison with canonical correlation decomposition further reveals differences between fixed-direction selection and correlation-based basis construction in the spatial structure and retention of flow information. Lag aggregation can improve structure identification when zero-lag association is insufficient. The gains depend on the cross-response distribution and window selection. TCC separates target-related ranking from mode-set construction, enabling comparison of spatial structures associated with different observables within the same modal expansion.

papers.title: Phase-Matched Chirps for Energy-Efficient Excitation of Magneto-Mechanical Resonators
papers.summary: Magneto-mechanical resonators (MMRs) are a recently proposed class of passive, wireless devices used for sensing and tracking. The operating principle of MMRs relies on an excitation of the sensor by oscillating magnetic fields, followed by an inductive readout to measure the sensor's dynamics. One challenge lies in generating efficient excitation signals to ensure maximum energy harvesting by the sensor. In this simulation study, we focus on chirped magnetic-field excitations and compare their performance with conventional constant-frequency excitation for both sinusoidal and rectangular waveforms. The results indicate varying levels of efficiency, with a sinusoidal linear down-chirp excitation signal yielding the largest deflection angle, offering the best potential for reducing the energy consumption and improving the temporal resolution of the measurement.

papers.title: A New Twist on Astigmatic Transformation: Beyond Laguerre-Gaussian Beams
papers.summary: Astigmatic transformation is widely used to convert the azimuthal phase structure of Laguerre-Gaussian vortex beams into intensity patterns from which the topological charge can be read out. Here, we show that this phase-to-intensity conversion is not just restricted to the Laguerre-Gaussian radial profile. We derive analytical expressions for the astigmatically transformed high-order Bessel--Gauss and perfect optical vortex fields, and find that, despite their substantially different radial structures, the number of intensity minima is directly set by the accumulated azimuthal phase winding. Numerical simulations and experimental measurements on both beam families confirm this result, establishing astigmatic transformation as a direct probe of the topological charge of scalar structured optical fields. We further extend the approach to non-separable vector Bessel-Gauss beams, in which the spatial and polarization degrees of freedom are coupled, and show that polarization-resolved detection allows the topological charge of the constituent spatial modes to be determined independently.

papers.title: Direct Production of Ultra-High Radioisotopic Pure $^{64}$Cu from Natural Zinc Metal via D-D Fusion Narrowband Fast Neutron Source Irradiation
papers.summary: Copper-64 radiopharmaceuticals have seen limited clinical deployment primarily due to the high cost of the isotopically enriched $^{64}$Ni metal required for its production. In this work we demonstrate that ultra-high radioisotopic pure $^{64}$Cu can be directly produced in a no-carrier-added-form from natural zinc metal through irradiation with D-D fusion narrowband fast neutron sources. A highly controlled D-D fusion narrowband fast neutron source at the ELI-ALPS Laser Facility was deployed to irradiate encapsulated 99.995\% pure natural zinc for 1 hour. Time-resolved gamma-ray spectroscopy of the irradiated sample over 72 hours was deployed to assess copper radioisotope activity. $^{64}$Cu was the only copper radioisotope detected within the irradiated sample, with a minimum and Minimum Detection Activity (MDA) threshold-corrected $^{64}$Cu radioisotopic purity of 99.62\% and 99.97\% respectively. Our result illustrates that highly controlled D-D fusion narrowband fast neutron sources have the potential to reduce the raw material production costs for $^{64}$Cu radiopharmaceuticals on the order of 2000 times. Cheaper $^{64}$Cu radiopharmaceuticals will increase their use in clinical practice, and, in-turn, increase outcomes for cancer patients receiving radionuclide therapy.

papers.title: A second-order linear decoupled scheme with a relaxed zero-energy variable for Rayleigh-B\'enard convection
papers.summary: We construct a second-order, linear, and fully decoupled scheme for Rayleigh--B\'enard convection between Navier-slip walls. The nonlinear terms are treated explicitly and multiplied by a scalar with exact value $1$ and no energy contributed to the continuous problem. As a result, each BDF2 step, with a rotational pressure correction, solves only constant-coefficient linear problems. For the time discretization, we prove that, for any time-step, the energy decays when the walls have equal temperatures, under a condition on the thermal weight, and the energy is bounded on finite time intervals when heated from below. Relaxing the scalar towards $1$ preserves both estimates. Energy stability does not control the accuracy of the scalar; the velocity and temperature fields are computed with its unrelaxed value, whose deviation from $1$ scales like $(E/C)(\delta t/\tau)^3$ for kinetic energy $E$, time-scale $\tau$ of the flow, and weight $C$ of the scalar equation. In our tests, choosing $C$ comparable to $E$ keeps this deviation small and doubles the largest time-step for which steady rolls are reproduced to a relative difference of $10^{-8}$. With Taylor--Hood elements, we observe second-order convergence in time, recover the critical Rayleigh numbers, and match published Nusselt numbers to within $0.5\%$. A three-dimensional implementation passes corresponding validation tests.
